key_insight: A principled diffusion-based data assimilation framework can fuse sparse observations with physics in clean-state space while explicitly using the prescribed observation-error covariance via an ensemble Kalman update.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more Bayesian route to reconstructing turbulent flow states from sparse measurements, with potential value for forecasting, control, and digital twins where full-field simulation is too costly.
method: Assimilate observations in the clean-state space rather than directly in noisy latent space
Use an ensemble Kalman update to inject the observation-error covariance explicitly
Leverage diffusion models as the generative prior for physically plausible flow fields
evidence_signal: On Lorenz-63, the method achieved lower trajectory error and equation residual than other diffusion-based posterior samplers, and on 2D Rayleigh-Bénard convection it matched large-scale DNS statistics with differences mainly at smaller scales.
watch_item: The ensemble underestimates posterior uncertainty, so uncertainty quantification may be overconfident and needs further calibration.
paper_title: Toward Principled Generative Data Assimilation of Turbulent Flows from Sparse Observations
